selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the story, what did the king give to each of the two men?
questions.answer: A piece of land with useful things to work with.

questions.question: What did the two men do at first with the estates?
questions.answer: They held them in their care.

questions.question: What might happen to things in that dangerous time?
questions.answer: They might be destroyed or changed.

questions.question: What promise did the king make about the future of the estate?
questions.answer: He would return it better after the troubles ended.

questions.question: What does the king’s offer show about his care for the men?
questions.answer: He wanted to help them, provide for them, and reward them.

questions.question: Why did the king say he should handle the big costs?
questions.answer: Because the men were too poor and weak to manage them.

questions.question: How did the wiser man answer the king’s message?
questions.answer: He gladly accepted and gave thanks.

questions.question: What new role would the accepting man receive?
questions.answer: He would become a respected soldier of the king.

questions.question: Which man accepted the offer with gratitude?
questions.answer: The smart man.

questions.question: How many men are in the comparison?
questions.answer: Two men.

questions.question: Why did the king send a trusted helper to the two men?
questions.answer: To give them the king’s message with mercy and care.

questions.question: Why is that condition important for understanding the king’s message?
questions.answer: It explains why the property was in danger.

questions.question: What was the king’s offer about the entrusted property?
questions.answer: If they gave it back to him, he would keep it safe for them.

questions.question: Why did the king say the men needed his help?
questions.answer: They did not have enough power or wealth for such big work.

questions.question: What would they lose besides the property if they refused?
questions.answer: They would lose the special payment and profit.

questions.question: What two losses did the king warn about if they did not accept?
questions.answer: They would lose the property and lose the offered reward.

questions.question: How is the second man described before he answers?
questions.answer: As proud, selfish, and wasteful.

questions.question: What happened to the wise man later?
questions.answer: He gained honor and a happy life with the king.

questions.question: At the beginning, what did each man receive from the king?
questions.answer: An estate with equipment, animals, and weapons.

questions.question: Were things in that time safe and lasting, or shaky and changing?
questions.answer: They were shaky and changing.

questions.question: Why did the king want them to give it back to him?
questions.answer: So he could protect it and keep it from being lost.

questions.question: What was the main choice put before the two men?
questions.answer: Whether to give the property back to the king or not.

questions.question: How did the king plan to reward the use of the tools?
questions.answer: He would give a much bigger payment.

questions.question: Which man made the wise choice?
questions.answer: The thoughtful one did.
